title: Kestrel and the Ghost
premise: Kestrel Sterling, a disgraced intelligence analyst, receives a calendar invite from her handler Marcus Vane—sent two days after his confirmed death. Following the digital trail, she uncovers a buried program called GLASSHOUSE in which the three agencies that fired her laundered fabricated intelligence to justify a covert war. Hunted by an assassin who knows her tradecraft because he was trained by the same program, Kestrel must decide whether loyalty to the people who discarded her is worth more than the truth that could destroy them. In the end she exposes GLASSHOUSE at terrible personal cost, learns Vane faked his death to protect her, and chooses exile over rejoining the system that made her.
about_author: O. M. Eastwick is the pen name of a former policy researcher who spent a decade writing classified-adjacent reports before turning to fiction. Eastwick lives quietly on the coast and refuses interviews, citing a fondness for being unfindable.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Ten years after her third dismissal, Kestrel lives deliberately small in Lisbon until a calendar ping arrives from dead handler Marcus Vane: a meeting tomorrow, coordinates attached. Checking the metadata, she finds it was scheduled before his death. The beat is unease curdling into compulsion—the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She goes to the meeting point, a shuttered archive annex, and finds Vane absent but a burner phone taped beneath a chair, preloaded with one file fragment labeled GLASSHOUSE. A watcher photographs her from across the street. The beat is dread: she realizes accepting the invitation made her visible again.

chapters.title: Three Names
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with the assassin, Codename Lark. Kestrel decodes the fragment into three names—officials across three governments who co-signed the program. Meanwhile Lark receives his contract: not the names, but Kestrel herself. The beat is converging threat, two hunters circling the same secret from opposite sides.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Wasn't Fired
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She tracks down former colleague Priya Nair, supposedly dismissed alongside her, and discovers Priya never existed—her identity was manufactured as cover. Confronting Priya yields a partial confession about fabricated intelligence feeds. The beat is betrayal; even Kestrel's memories of camaraderie were staged.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Lark's POV. Lark closes in but hesitates when he recognizes Kestrel's tradecraft as GLASSHOUSE-trained—he was taught by the same instructors. He reports a false negative to buy time, corrupting himself for the first time. The beat is the assassin's mirror-moment: the target reflects what he might have become.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Live Wire
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Using the burner, Kestrel reaches someone claiming to be Vane—voice scrambled, location spoofed. He tells her the truth must go public within nine days or the program's architects will bury it with a new war. The beat is resolve hardening into mission; she stops running and starts planning.

chapters.title: The Long Corridor
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel smuggles herself into an interagency summit via Priya's manufactured credentials, copying the GLASSHOUSE ledger mid-ceremony. She is nearly caught by the deputy director who once fired her—and who she now realizes signed everything. The beat is vertigo at the summit of power: corruption wearing institutional medals.

chapters.title: Lark Descending
chapters.summary: Lark's POV. His handlers discover his false report and send a cleanup team after them both. Lark breaks cover to warn Kestrel, and the two fugitives compare scars from the same program. The beat is unlikely alliance—loyalty redirected from institution to person, at the cost of everything either had left.

chapters.title: Glasshouse
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, climax. Cornered in a decommissioned listening station, Kestrel broadcasts the ledger to press contacts in all three countries while Lark holds off the cleanup team. Vane appears in person—alive, having engineered everything to force her hand. The beat is catharsis through exposure: truth delivered past every gatekeeper, whatever it costs next.

chapters.title: After the Fall
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, resolution. Governments scramble, careers burn, and Kestrel declines reinstatement offers from every agency that once discarded her. She meets Lark one last time before they vanish along separate roads. Final beat: quiet sovereignty—she keeps neither revenge nor redemption, only the self she refused to surrender.
